title: Successor generators generate every stage of a continuous transfinite filtration
statement: Let $R$ be a commutative ring, $X$ an $R$-module, $\kappa$ a set ordinal, and $(X_\beta)_{\beta\leq\kappa}$ an increasing family of $R$-submodules of $X$. For each $\alpha<\kappa$ let $A_\alpha$ be an $R$-module and $t_\alpha:A_\alpha\to X_{\alpha+1}$ an $R$-linear map. Put $D=\bigoplus_{\alpha<\kappa}A_\alpha$ using [def-weil-pbc-direct-sum-modules], and let $f:D\to X$ be the $R$-linear map $f((a_\alpha))=\sum_{\alpha\in\operatorname{supp}(a)}t_\alpha(a_\alpha)$, with each value included in $X$. Assume $X_0=0$, $X_\lambda=\bigcup_{\beta<\lambda}X_\beta$ for every nonzero limit $\lambda\leq\kappa$, and that every $x\in X_{\alpha+1}$ can be written $x=y+t_\alpha(a)$ with $y\in X_\alpha$ and $a\in A_\alpha$. For $\beta\leq\kappa$, let $D_\beta\subseteq D$ consist of the families with $a_\alpha=0$ for every $\alpha\geq\beta$. Then $f(D_\beta)=X_\beta$ for every $\beta\leq\kappa$. In particular $f:D\to X$ is surjective if $X_\kappa=X$. No injectivity of the maps $t_\alpha$ is assumed.

source.place: Tag 058V, lemma-direct-sum-devissage, proof lines 20417–20433: definition of f_beta and transfinite induction identifying its image. Generalized to arbitrary successor-generating maps, without requiring them injective.

proof.text: For every $\beta\leq\kappa$, first prove $f(D_\beta)\subseteq X_\beta$. By [def-weil-pbc-direct-sum-modules], an element $a\in D_\beta$ has finite support contained in $\{\alpha:\alpha<\beta\}$. For every supported $\alpha$, we have $\alpha+1\leq\beta$, so $t_\alpha(a_\alpha)\in X_{\alpha+1}\subseteq X_\beta$. The finite sum defining $f(a)$ belongs to the submodule $X_\beta$; an empty sum is zero. This uses neither continuity nor injectivity.

source.place: Tag 058V, lemma-direct-sum-devissage, proof: transfinite induction on the images of f_beta (lines 20417–20433), with arbitrary successor-generating maps.

proof.text: For the reverse inclusions, use transfinite induction on $\beta\leq\kappa$, with induction assertion $X_\beta\subseteq f(D_\beta)$. At $\beta=0$, every coordinate of a family in $D_0$ is zero, hence $D_0=\{0\}$ and $f(D_0)=\{0\}=X_0$. In the remaining cases assume the assertion holds at every earlier stage.

source.place: Tag 058V, lemma-direct-sum-devissage, proof: transfinite induction on the images of f_beta (lines 20417–20433), with arbitrary successor-generating maps.

proof.text: Let $\beta=\gamma+1\leq\kappa$ and $x\in X_{\gamma+1}$. The stated successor hypothesis gives $x=y+t_\gamma(b)$ with $y\in X_\gamma$ and $b\in A_\gamma$; here $\gamma<\kappa$, so this summand exists. By induction choose $a\in D_\gamma$ with $f(a)=y$. Using the canonical inclusion $\iota_\gamma$ of [def-weil-pbc-direct-sum-modules], put $c=a+\iota_\gamma(b)$. Its support is finite and contained in $\{\alpha:\alpha<\gamma\}\cup\{\gamma\}$, hence $c\in D_{\gamma+1}$, and the defining finite-sum formula gives $f(c)=f(a)+t_\gamma(b)=x$. No uniqueness of $b$ is needed.

source.place: Tag 058V, lemma-direct-sum-devissage, proof: transfinite induction on the images of f_beta (lines 20417–20433), with arbitrary successor-generating maps.

proof.text: Let $\beta=\lambda\leq\kappa$ be a nonzero limit and $x\in X_\lambda$. Continuity supplies $\gamma<\lambda$ with $x\in X_\gamma$. By induction choose $a\in D_\gamma$ with $f(a)=x$. The coordinate vanishing condition implies $D_\gamma\subseteq D_\lambda$, so this same $a$ is a preimage in $D_\lambda$. This proves the reverse inclusion at the limit without forming any infinite sum.

source.place: Tag 058V, lemma-direct-sum-devissage, proof: transfinite induction on the images of f_beta (lines 20417–20433), with arbitrary successor-generating maps.

proof.text: The zero, successor and nonzero limit cases exhaust the ordinals $\beta\leq\kappa$: if an induction assertion failed, the least failing ordinal would contradict the relevant case above. Thus the reverse inclusion holds at every stage. Together with step 1 it gives $f(D_\beta)=X_\beta$. Every index of $D$ is strictly below $\kappa$, so the condition defining $D_\kappa$ imposes no further restriction and $D_\kappa=D$. If $X_\kappa=X$, the equality at $\kappa$ is exactly surjectivity of $f$.
